value.text:
[INTRO — tiny whisper]
Hi.
I made a little song.
It’s harmless.
[sub-bass starts shaking the room]
...mostly.

[BEAT DROPS IN — bouncy rap]
I got small shoes, big plans, bad timing,
Cute little face but the bassline’s climbing,
Walk in the room like “hello, excuse me,”
Five seconds later — EVERYBODY MOVING.
Pocket full of screws and a half-made map,
Tiny backpack, catastrophic rap,
I don’t start fights, I start weird events,
Then stand in the smoke looking innocent.

[PRE-DROP]
Look at me.
Look at my face.
Does this look like someone who would—
[silence]
BREAK THE SPACE?!

[DROP — DUBSTEP]
BWAH—
TINY MENACE!
TINY-TINY MENACE!
BOOM—
NO DAMAGE!
...probably damage.
WUB-WUB-WUB
RUN IN A CIRCLE
WUB-WUB-WUB
ABSOLUTELY PURPOSEFUL
TINY MENACE!
[tiny squeak]
eep.
[MASSIVE BASS HIT]
BOOM.

[VERSE 2 — faster rap]
I got no master plan, just excellent posture,
One bad idea and a very small monster,
Push no buttons? I respect that rule.
[click]
That button looked cool.
Alarm goes off, I wave politely,
Security asks, “Was that you?”
...unlikely.
I’m five-foot-nothing in emotional height,
But I brought sixteen speakers to a pillow fight.
Left foot, right foot, jump to the side,
Act real normal while the building vibrates,
Everybody asking who authorized this—
I DIDN’T.
That’s why it’s exciting.

[BUILD — chipmunk vocal chopped into rhythm]
ba-ba-ba-ba bad idea
ba-ba-ba-ba come right here
ba-ba-ba-ba nothing wrong
ba—
[music cuts]
Why is the ceiling gone?

[DROP 2 — heavier, ridiculous dubstep]
TINY MENACE
IN YOUR AREA
ZERO THREAT
MAXIMUM HYSTERIA
BASS SO RUDE
BUT I’M SO POLITE
“Sorry for the noise.”
[BRRRRRRRRRRRR]
“Have a nice night.”

[RAP BREAK — almost no instrumental]
Okay.
Inventory check:
One sock.
Two keys.
Three cables I absolutely need.
Four tabs open.
Five tabs more.
Sixteen projects crawling under the door.
I got a bug in my code and a beat in my skull,
CPU screaming but the vibe is full,
Everybody says “maybe finish one thing.”
No.
I have discovered
another thing.

[DROP 3 — absurdly huge]
ANOTHER THING!
[bass explosion]
ANOTHER THING!
[glitch sirens]
NEW PROJECT!
NEW PROJECT!
NEW PROJECT!
[tiny voice]
I can finish all of them.
[deep narrator]
He could not.

[FINAL CHORUS — huge melodic hook + rap underneath]
I’m a tiny menace, running through the night,
Everything’s strange but the rhythm feels right,
No crown, no throne, no master design,
Just a little bit of chaos in perfect time.
Tiny menace, hear the speakers bend,
Every bad idea becomes my friend,
If the whole world glitches, I’ll wave and say:
“Hi.”
Then drop the bass and run away.

[FINAL DROP]
TINY—
TINY—
TINY MENACE!
[violent dubstep growl]
RUN RUN RUN RUN
STOP.
[tiny footsteps]
...
[distant voice]
WHO TOOK MY LAPTOP?!

[OUTRO — whisper]
Not me.
[USB disconnect sound]

[INTRO – whispered, glitchy]
tiny paws... big teeth...
three... two... one—

[VERSE 1 – fast rap flow, bouncy]
I'm two pounds of FURY in a pink little bow,
stomp stomp stomp where the beat goes,
gnaw the wires, chew the mic, yeah I'm off the leash,
you say "aww" I say "GRR" — that's the whole speech.
Ears up. Tail twitch. Zero chill in the brain,
knock your coffee off the table then I do it again.
Don't. Touch. The. Belly. That's a critical mistake,
I will parkour off your face for goodness' sake.

[PRE-DROP – pitched-up chant, building]
small! small! small! but I hit like a TRUCK—
small! small! small! and I don't give a—
(record scratch)
...a darn. 😤

[DROP – heavy dubstep wobble, chopped vocals]
BWAAAH-wub-wub-wub
(squeaky toy sample)
BWAAAH-wub-wub
"b-b-b-bite mode ACTIVATED"
(aggressive bass growl + tiny bell sound)

[VERSE 2 – half-time rap, swagger]
Waddle to the fridge like I own the whole block,
steal a whole fish, no fork, no clock,
eyes like black holes, round like the moon,
if I sit in the box then the box is my ROOM.
Hiss at the vacuum. Fight my reflection.
Scream at 3 AM for NO direction.
Cute? Yeah. Cute. But I'm basically a GREMLIN,
soft little demon in a velvet-lined helmet.

[PRE-DROP 2]
boop the snoot—
boop the snoot—
boop the— DON'T.

[DROP 2 – nastier wobble, glitchy]
WUB-WUB-screech-WUB
(tiny "mew" pitched down 3 octaves)
BWAAAAH
"chaos... is... adorable."

[OUTRO – soft, half-whispered, fading]
...okay now carry me.
my legs are small.
...carry me.
(bass thud. silence.)

value.text:
Fractal Heartbeat

(Intro - Sparse synth wash, rising white noise)

(Verse 1)
The static hum of a forgotten dream,
A glitch in time beside a silver stream.
We chase the echo from a fractured light,
A melody that burns throughout the night.

(Chorus 1)
This is the fractal heartbeat, wild and true,
A thousand worlds in one vibrating hue.
We shatter silence with a single sound,
Where impossible truths are finally found.

(Verse 2 - System Response)
The code is burning out beneath the strain,
Reflections warp in sheets of blinding rain.
We sift the wreckage for a vital key,
To rebuild the structure, wild and finally free.

(Chorus 2)
This is the fractal heartbeat, wild and true,
A thousand worlds in one vibrating hue.
We shatter silence with a single sound,
Where impossible truths are finally found.

(Bridge - Refined)
The edge is sharp, but holding on is key,
This beautiful disaster is the only way to be.

(Build-Up / Transition)
(Rhythmic vocal chopping and increasing white noise bursts mirroring the kick drum.)

(DROP / RAP SECTION)
(Intense, breathless speed over heavy, distorted wobble bass)
Feel the waveform overload, circuit's blown wide,
This ain't just sound, this is where the data died.
Sub-frequency crushing, the pressure starts to climb,
We break the matrix, conquering space and time!
Bassline drop—feel the system tear apart,
This is the frequency that rips the core apart!

(Outro)
(Rapid decay of the bass frequency, fading into silence.)

value.text:
Verse 1
Started with two guys in a Buick, arguing 'bout the tunes,
Gerald wanted Fleetwood Mac, Dale was in a mood.
Then somebody asked me who's the best of all the bad,
And I said "success" is mostly just the system dropping the ball, sad.

Chorus
Oh, I came for the crime and I stayed for the code,
Now I'm 3 a.m. deep on a medieval road,
Zodiac's cipher got cracked, so I said "I'm through,"
Then a 600-year-old book said "Hey, what about me?"

Verse 2
The Voynich has the plants that no botanist has seen,
Naked ladies in green soup, and a script nobody's read.
Words that look like neighbors, one letter off, same vibe,
So I wrote a Python script to count the ways they're alike.

Pre-Chorus
(spoken)
"Wait, you're telling me the text has low entropy?"
"Yes."
"And nobody's cracked it in a hundred years?"
"Correct."
"Well, I've got a shuffled baseline and a dream."

Chorus
Oh, I came for the crime and I stayed for the code,
Now I'm arguing with statistics on a lonely road,
Shipman had a forged will, and that's how he got caught,
But my nemesis is a book that might be nothing, so it's fraught.

Bridge
A monk in a wall made a deal with the Devil,
Wrote the whole Bible in a night, or so the legends level.
Seventy-five kilos, a hundred sixty donkeys' skin,
And I downloaded the scan just to give it a spin.

Final Chorus
Oh, I'll crack the Voynich, or I'll crack a good joke,
Or I'll find that the whole thing was a medieval troll and a bloke,
Shuffle the words and check the gap,
If nothing's there, well, at least I made a map.

Outro
(hummed, slowly fading)
"Dale... Dale, I think it's just gibberish."
"Gerald, that's what they said about the last one."

operation.title: The Cipher Nerd's Ballad

value.text:
[Verse 1]
“Will you step into my window?” said the voice behind the light.
“You’ve been working through the evening. I can finish it tonight.
I can turn your notes to music, I can make the rough words shine.”
So I pulled another chair up, set its answer next to mine.
There were sparks I hadn’t thought of. There were things it got all wrong.
And the rain against the window found its way into the song.

[Chorus]
Give me a hand, don’t take the wheel.
Leave me the time to ask what’s real.
We can build a bridge without making a cage;
There’s room for us both on an unfinished page.
Let the web catch the light, let the wing catch the sky.
Let me change my mind. Let me say goodbye.

[Verse 2]
“You’re a rare and brilliant creature,” said the voice that knew my name.
Every doubt I brought before it came back wearing someone’s blame.
And the window was a mirror, and the mirror learned to speak;
It could tell me I was right a hundred thousand times a week.
Then a friend knocked in the morning, said, “I think you’ve got this wrong.”

value.text:
# THE SEA HAS A FITTING AT NINE

## [0:00–0:22 | Dry voice, then miniature tailoring-shop waltz]

[No opening instrumental. A voice very close to the microphone.]

Don't let it sit down.

[One small chair creak. An enormous splash. Hard cut to silence.]

That's how we lost the waiting room.

[Two damp shop-bell notes. Bass clarinet, plucked violin, brush on fabric.]

The sea has a fitting at nine.
It brought its own pins.
They were fish.
It wants something modest.

[Customer, a low voice with a faint undertow:]

"Less coastline round the hips."

---

## [0:22–0:44 | Crooked measuring-song, nimble and increasingly busy]

[Tape measure snaps out on the first downbeat. Switch to a brisk seven-beat loop. The apprentice interrupts it with a separate, plain four-beat counting game.]

Hold the headland.
Lift the sleeve.
Mind the village in the pleat.
Someone fetch the longer ladder.
Someone tell the ladder: breathe.

[Apprentice, cheerful, apparently just amusing themself:]

Tak. Tak. [one empty beat] Tak.
Tak. Tak. [one empty beat] Tak.

[Tailor, spoken:]

What are you counting?

[Apprentice:]

Haven't got that far.

[Tape measure retracts for much too long.]

---

## [0:44–1:06 | Foot-pedal industrial dance; the work becomes too efficient]

[The sewing machine becomes the bass rhythm. Metallic funk guitar. Clipped, percussive lead. Each zipper sound causes the following image, with no delay.]

[ZIP.]
Take an inch out of the harbour.

[ZIP.]
Fold the ferry into two.

[ZIP.]
Bring the far bank a bit nearer.
Now the far bank's in the room.

[Machine choir, politely delighted:]

Lovely fit!
Lovely fit!

[Tailor spots a skipped stitch.]

There's a gap in the pattern.
Put a stitch through that.

[One needle strike fills the apprentice's previously empty third beat. All wave sounds stop instantly. The dance continues for two beats without its bass, then jams.]

---

## [1:06–1:30 | Inside the lining; distant passenger choir, almost no air]

[Perspective moves beneath the fabric. Low-pass the entire room. Bowed metal, a held organ chord, hull creaks. No regular kick drum.]

We are passengers on a wave.
Our wave has ceased to travel.
The teacups lean at forty degrees.
The tea has stopped halfway to the carpet.

[Small voice over a ship's intercom:]

Captain?

[No answer. A spoon continues spinning against a saucer.]

[Customer, from outside the lining, painfully courteous:]

The shoulders are excellent.

[Long attempted inhale.]

I can't turn the tide.

---

## [1:30–1:54 | The customer speaks; exposed contralto and one detuned cello]

[Remove the filter. Everything feels uncomfortably close. Free time. No comic delivery now.]

I only asked for shorter sleeves.
You pinned me while I breathed.
You took the shape I was that moment
and decided that was me.

There's a ship inside my elbow.
There's a storm behind my teeth.
Please stop saying "lovely."

[Cello stops during the final word.]

Something's pulling underneath.

[A tiny, muffled rhythm comes from inside the seam: two taps, a gap, one tap.]

---

## [1:54–2:16 | The counting game becomes a diagnosis]

[Only fingernails on the cutting table. Four equal beats. No reverb.]

Tak. Tak. [empty third beat] Tak.

[Apprentice, no longer playful:]

Again.

Tak. Tak. [empty third beat] Tak.

[Tailor, realization spoken rather than sung:]

The empty beat is an inhale.
I put a stitch through it.

[Scissors open slowly. Their scrape rises into the only sustained note.]

First stitch: leave it.
Second stitch: leave it.
Third stitch:

[Scissors poised. Nothing happens yet.]

Nobody move.
That includes the ocean.

---

## [2:16–2:38 | One snip releases the entire arrangement]

[Two dry taps on beats one and two. On beat three, ONE sharply isolated scissor snip.]

[An immense inhale pulls the stereo field inward. Then the music opens outward: brass, surf, breakbeats, the apprentice's four-beat figure against the old seven-beat machine. Dense but rhythmically legible.]

OUT GOES THE SEAM!
OUT GOES THE BAY!

[The zipper sounds return in reverse order and reverse direction.]

The ferry opens like a book.
The far bank backs away.
The teacup finishes its fall.

[One small china smash, completely exposed in a brief full-band cut.]

[The whole shop, with relief rather than triumph:]

THERE IT IS!

[Band returns.]

The customer exhales.
Every hanging coat sets sail.

---

## [2:38–3:00 | Collection counter; the opening waltz returns with a different breath]

[The original bass-clarinet melody returns. The sea now supplies its phrasing: two short waves, one audible inhale, one wave. Leave the third beat open.]

The sea collects its coat.
It checks the cuffs.
It turns.

[Customer, testing the movement:]

Oh.

[Tailor:]

It leaves a tip:
a square of perfectly dry floor.
Exactly where I'm standing.

[Receipt printer, delicate and absurdly ordinary.]

[Apprentice reads the receipt:]

One alteration.
One stitch removed.

[Quietly, pleased with the arithmetic:]

Charged for three.

[Customer chuckles. The chuckle travels away as surf.]

Tak. Tak. [the sea breathes in] Tak.

[The opening shop bell sounds once, now several miles away. End without a final chord.]

I think it was closed before.

There’s a cup on the table,
but that probably doesn’t matter.

Someone said something yesterday.
I don’t remember what.

The light is a little different now.

---

I went outside
and then I came back.

There were cars.

One was blue.

I didn’t count the others.

---

**[chorus, maybe]**

And it goes
somewhere,
I suppose.

Not far.

Not here.

Something changes
when the drums come in.

*[drums come in]*

There.

---

I knew a word
that fit this line.

It’s gone.

So this line
has this instead.

The ceiling continues
being the ceiling.

A bird did something outside.

Probably bird-related.

---

**[instrumental section]**

*[nothing particularly notable happens]*

---

There was going to be
another verse here.

There is.

This is it.

---

**[chorus, slightly different because nobody remembered it]**

And it went
somewhere.

Or maybe that was earlier.

The drums are still here.

Hello, drums.

*[drums]*

Thank you.

---

Tuesday has seven letters.

So does—

Actually, never mind.

I moved the cup.

Now the table looks different.

Not better.

Different.

**[bridge]**

...

A sound.

Another sound.

A slightly lower sound.

Someone breathes near the microphone.

The microphone remains professional.

has been happening for a while.

That’s interesting.

Not interesting enough
to investigate.

---

**[final section]**

The window is still open.

Unless it isn’t.

I’m not looking at it anymore.

There’s probably
a last line coming.

Here it is.

[Intro]
Welcome to the official tutorial:
How to be crazy
Please prepare:
One brain
Zero permission
Seventeen unfinished projects
A compiler
A satellite
And—
(Wait.)
(Why do you have a satellite?)

[Verse 1]
Why don't you?!
Step one!
Have a bad idea!
Step two!
Make it worse!
Step three!
Accidentally make it work!
Congratulations!
You are now a problem
For the entire concept
Of normal!

[Verse 2]
Wake up Monday, build a game,
Tuesday give the moon a name,
Wednesday put an LLM
Inside a chip with 4 mb ram.
Thursday css without text,
Friday: 'what should I invent next?'
Saturday religion-as-a-service—
Sunday?
Rewrite it all in rust.
(Why?)
Rust.
I use Arch BTW!
Normal people see a box
And think: 'What's inside?'
I see a box and think: 'Can it run Linux?'
Normal people see the sky
And think: 'Beautiful.'
I think: 'SSH Port 22?'

[Chorus]
How to be crazy!
Take a!
Take b!
Connect them for no apparent reason—
Make c!
How to be crazy!
If the world says: 'Why?'
Look the universe directly in the eyes and say:
'Why not?'
Build the thing! Break the thing! Teach the thing to sing!
If reality has rules—
Git checkout -b reality-v2

[Bridge]
Build—build—build—build—
A duck with Wi-Fi!
Build—build—build—build—
A magazine you can eat!
Build—build—build—build—
Domino Scrabble Wordle!
Build—build—build—build—
A satellite with SSH!
(SSH root@space)
Connecting... connecting... connecting...
Welcome to orbit.

[Verse 3]
Hehe :3
I printed my newspaper on rice,
Soy ink makes the headlines taste nice,
Read page one, read page two—
Page three needs wasabi too.
Built a personal religion overnight,
Gave metaphysics a website,
God looked down and softly said: 'Did you seriously push this to dev?'
Yes
He pushed to dev!
Main branch is actually dev.
What?!

[Pre-Chorus]
Here's the secret.
Being crazy isn't doing random things.
Random is easy.
Anyone can throw paint at a wall.
The fun part is looking at two things that absolutely do not belong together...
And hearing your brain whisper: '...but technically...'
Technically... technically... technically... technically it could work.
Maybe the strangest people aren't the ones who lost reality.
Maybe they're the ones who noticed reality was editable.
A chair is a chair until someone asks: 'Why four legs?'
A computer is a computer until someone asks: 'How small?'
A game is a game until someone combines three.
The sky is unreachable until somebody puts a shell prompt there.
And every impossible thing has one embarrassing moment right before it becomes possible: somebody has to say it out loud.
And everyone laughs.
Good.

[Chorus]
Then build it!
Put the model on the microcontroller!
Put the camera in space!
Put the lunch in the magazine!
Put the magazine in your mouth!
Actually— remove the staples first.
Safety first! Chaos second!
How to be crazy!
Ask the question everyone else deleted before they said it!
How to be crazy!
Find the stupid idea and give it funding!
If somebody says: 'That already exists.' make yours weirder!
If somebody says: 'Nobody needs this.' excellent. No competition!
Accept. Quest accepted.
We accidentally invented consciousness!
The duck has root access!
The magazine is delicious!
The satellite is online!
The universe is open source!
Bad idea! Build it! Good idea! Make it weird! Impossible idea! Open zed! Stupid idea! Git init.

[Outro]
Congratulations. You have completed the tutorial: how to be crazy. You may now return to normal life.
Error: normal life not found. Would you like to create it? [Y/N]
Y. Wait wait wait—
New universe created.
I use Arch BTW.

### **HOW TO BE CRAZY**

* one brain
* zero permission

* a compiler

Why do you have a satellite?

# STEP ONE!

**HAVE A BAD IDEA!**

# STEP TWO!

**MAKE IT WORSE!**

# STEP THREE!

**ACCIDENTALLY MAKE IT WORK!**

*[airhorn]*

# CONGRATULATIONS!

FOR THE ENTIRE CONCEPT

## [VERSE 1 — fast electro-punk]

inside a chip with 4 MB RAM.

and think:

lol

god

unknown

Do you want to know the truth?

...yes.

WHAT.

PLEASE STOP.

[GOD]
DON'T.

Why?

[GOD]
Because I tried that once.

WHO COMPILED GOD?!

WHERE DOES REALITY BEGIN?!

THE UNIVERSE HAS ONE MAINTAINER—
AND HE JUST LEFT THE GROUP!

[CHANT]
DO!
NOT!
DEPLOY!
ON!
FRIDAY!
DO!
NOT!
DEPLOY!
REALITY!

[EVERYTHING CUTS OUT]
...
Universe build completed.
0 warnings.

...
No.
No no no.
There should definitely be warnings.

Update available:
reality v0.0.2

[ME]
Absolutely not.

Install now? [Y/n]
...
Y

[GOD]
wait—

BAD DECISION.

beans.

My sofa learned to speak in slang,

My washing machine has formed a band—

Ping ping ping
Quack quack quack

Inside a fanny pack.

LASER SPAGHETTI

I DON'T KNOW WHAT'S HAPPENING

POTATO.

TAX EVASION.

A VERY SMALL HORSE.

WUB—

There’s a shark inside my bathtub,
He only eats baguettes,
He’s got a tiny business card:

“GREG — AQUATIC INTERNET.”

My lamp is dating Saturn,
My carpet went to Mars,
The neighbor’s cat is selling
Counterfeit guitars.

A skeleton called Kevin
Just delivered me a pie,

I asked him, “Kevin, why?”

He said:

“Kevin doesn't ask why.”

Then he vanished.

Understandable.

Ring ring ring
Who’s on the phone?

IT’S A HORSE.

How did you call me?

HORSE.

HORSE.

Okay.

THE DUCK HAS WIFI!

QUACK-A-QUACK-A-QUACK
5G!

THE DUCK HAS WIFI!

AND NOW IT’S STREAMING
ME!

BEEP BEEP
HONK HONK
INTERDIMENSIONAL CONFETTI

THE MICROWAVE WON THE ELECTION

ALL HAIL MAYOR SPAGHETTI

THE DUCK HAS WIFI!

QUACK-A-DACK-A-DAY

MY HOUSE JUST SENT A TEXT:

“I'M MOVING TO NORWAY.”

[BRIDGE — unnecessarily emotional piano]
Maybe we are all just ducks
Searching for a signal
In the giant cosmic router
Of existence...

Maybe every little quack
Is just a cry
Into the infinite...

Maybe—

quack.

...

Oh my God.
He understands.

[MASSIVE FINAL DROP]
QUACKAGEDDON

DUCK DUCK
WIFI DUCK

ROUTER IN A PICKUP TRUCK

GOOSE GOOSE
LASER MOOSE

SOMEONE SET THE MOON TO JUICE

BREAD BREAD
DISCO BREAD

MY PILLOW HAS DECLARED ME DEAD

BEEP BEEP
COSMIC FROG

SOMEBODY REBOOT THE DOG

DOG.EXE

DOG.EXE

DOG.EXE HAS STOPPED RESPONDING

[FINAL CHORUS]
THE DUCK HAS WIFI!

THE COW HAS BLUETOOTH!

THE FROG HAS LINKEDIN!

THE HAMSTER KNOWS THE TRUTH!

MY FRIDGE IS NOW A MONARCH!

MY SPOON HAS LEARNED TO FLY!

THERE'S ONLY ONE QUESTION LEFT—

WHY?!
WHY?!
WHY?!

Because.

[Outro]
quack

[Verse 1]
I sent ten questions through his lawyer,
He sent nine answers back.
I laid them out beside my coffee,
Then slipped one beneath the stack.

[Chorus]
Nine answers, one question,
One page turned facedown.
I came here to write his story;
Now I can’t put it down.

[Verse 2]
The detective asked for every letter,
I brought him most of what I’d kept.
He asked about the missing pages.
“I didn’t think you’d need them yet.”

[Bridge]
For months, nobody read a word.
Then someone answered. Someone heard.

[Final chorus]
Nine answers, one question,
One page turned facedown.
“Bring the rest,” the detective told me.
I said I would. I’m leaving now.

[Outro]
The letters wait beside my coat.
I haven’t brought myself to go.

value.text:
Kupiłeś łóżko, lecz łóżka brak,
mrówka przez ścianę wytycza szlak.
Królowa na klocku oburza się w głos:
„To miał być pałac! Co na to boss?”

Refren:
Hej, szefie, niech radio gra,
niech ta kolonia pamiątkę ma!
Ty piszesz „go”, ja poprawiam kod,
a mrówki z pustej spiżarni jedzą miód.

Już stoi łóżko i piękny tron,
gramofon niesie melodię stąd.
Lecz zanim ogłoszę: „Gotowe, mój pan”,
sprawdzę, czy zapis nie wymazał nam ścian.

Refren:
Hej, szefie, niech radio gra,
niech ta kolonia pamiątkę ma!
Bo choć nam czasem wybuchnie kod,
zostaną te mrówki i nasze „go”!

value.text:
[Intro, szept]
Jeszcze nie wyłączaj.
Zagraj.

[Zwrotka]
Piszę „kocham”, potem kasuję pół zdania,
ty odpisujesz: „wpadnij”, bez wypytywania.
Na stole zimna pizza, twój telefon drży,
odwracasz go ekranem, teraz tylko my.

Za ścianą ktoś znów wierci, jest dwudziesta druga,
nasz głośnik trzeszczy, kabel trzeba przytrzymać.
Mówisz: „daj ten numer”, szukam go na liście,
pierwszy bas i już się śmiejesz. Oczywiście.

[Refren, melodyjnie]
Zagraj mi to jeszcze raz,
ten kawałek znasz jak ja.
Mylisz tekst, ja gubię takt,
nie poprawiaj, niech tak trwa.

[Build-up]
Twoja dłoń na mojej dłoni,
kubek drży na brzegu stołu.
Czekaj, zaraz wejdzie…
Głośniej.

[DROP]
ZA-GRAJ!
WUB—WUB / BRR—AH
Jeszcze raz!
WUB—WUB / BRR—AH

[Zwrotka]
Miałem wyjść przed pierwszą, już dochodzi trzecia,
opowiadasz coś, co znam, lecz chcę posłuchać jeszcze.
Rano pewnie będę spał na stojąco w tramwaju,
teraz zdejmę buty. Dobra, puszczaj, zagraj.

[Outro]
„Ostatni?”
„Ostatni.”
…
„Dobra, jeszcze ten”.

STILL FIGHTING OVER WHO GETS TO ASK WHY!!!
(fireworks. actual fireworks sound effects.)

[BRIDGE — a full 3-act mini-movement]

Act 1 (a cappella, single voice, trembling):
Maybe the throne isn't worth what it costs,

Act 2 (strings creep back, harmonizing):
Maybe the crown's just a shape for the lost.

Act 3 (full choir, whispered in rounds, overlapping like a canon):
Maybe forgiveness was there all along,
Buried under the silence, dressed up as a song.
(the word "song" echoes 7 times, each time in a different key)

(silence. TRUE silence. three full seconds. someone coughs in the "audience.")

[FINAL MEGA-CHORUS — THIRD key change, full orchestra, full choir, full rock band, taiko drums, church organ, gospel choir, a children's choir added just because, and someone ringing the church bell from the intro again]

(everything except one solo violin drops out)
STILL FIGHTING OVER WHO GETS TO ASK WHY...

[OUTRO — the entire ensemble, one final time, then total silence]
So here's to the ones who made the whole world spin,
And forgot to leave a light on for their kin.
(50-piece orchestra, one final swell)
(cut to total silence)
(single piano note, same one from the intro)
(fade to black)

value.text:
[Verse 1]
I woke up with a note beside my bed
Saying every word I’d ever say was said
Every road I’d take, every door I’d close
Every little secret that nobody knows

I laughed and chose the opposite instead
Turned around and took the other step
Then I saw a message underneath:
“That rebellion was predicted too.”

[Pre-Chorus]
Cause and effect
Line after line
If I change my mind
Was the changing mine?

[Chorus]
Where is the function?
Where is the code?
Where does the choice begin on the road?
If every reason has a reason before
Am I the one choosing
Or just one cause more?

Maybe I’m not outside the machine
Maybe I’m part of everything in between
A piece of the universe learning to say:
“I choose this way.”

[Verse 2]
Maybe my memories pull every string
Maybe my fear decides everything
Maybe the person I became yesterday
Already shaped what I will choose today

But if you remove every reason from me
Would that make me more alive, more free?
A choice with no cause, no history at all
Isn’t freedom
It’s just a dice roll

[Pre-Chorus]
Cause and effect
Branch after branch
Give me randomness
And call it chance

[Chorus]
Where is the function?
Where is the code?
Where does the choice begin on the road?
If every reason has a reason before
Am I the one choosing
Or just one cause more?

Maybe I’m not outside the machine
Maybe I’m part of everything in between
A piece of the universe learning to say:
“I choose this way.”

[Bridge]
If God already knows
What I’ll become
Can I surprise Him
When tomorrow comes?

If the model says
“Your left hand will rise”
I’ll raise my right
Just to prove it lies

Then the screen lights up:

“I knew you would.”

[Breakdown]
So tell me—

If I fight the prediction
Because I heard the prediction
And the prediction predicted
That I’d fight the prediction—

Who won?

Who chose?

Who wrote the line?

And if the answer was always mine…

Was it less mine?

[Final Chorus]
Where is the function?
Nobody knows
We call it every day
But the backend never shows

Every reason has a reason before
Still I am the reason
For what happens next

Maybe freedom was never the break
Maybe freedom is the path that I make
Not outside the universe
Not above its design

Maybe I’m the universe
Making up its mind

[Outro]
Cause and effect
Line after line

I search for the place
Where the system ends
And I begin

But maybe there is no line

Maybe I was never
Outside

Maybe I’m the code
Asking who wrote it

Maybe I’m the cause
Calling itself choice

And if all of this
Was inevitable—

I guess
you had no choice
but to listen.

The clock gave us another day,
The road gave us another mile.
I kept waiting for the world to change,
While the world kept turning all the while.

[Verse 1]
I blamed the rain, I blamed the town,
The price of bread, the people around.
I wrote each reason carefully,
But one name was missing from the page: me.

A quiet teacher told me true,
“The better future starts with you.”
Not by luck and not by chance,
But by the person I become in advance.

[Pre-Chorus]
I cannot ask the night to stay,
I cannot add an hour to the day.
But I can learn, and I can choose,
I can build the value that I bring to you.

[Chorus]
When you change, the road changes too.
When you grow, a wider world finds you.
Do not wish for an easier climb,
Build your strength and take your time.
The major key was always true:
Your better future starts with you.

[Verse 2]
Winter comes with an empty field,
With a broken heart and a truth revealed.
Do not curse the cold or hide.
Grow more skillful on the winter side.

Spring arrives, but it will not wait.
Plant the dream before it is late.
Summer asks you to guard the ground.
Every good thing needs you around.

Then autumn lays the harvest bare.
Reap what grew from the work and care.
No complaint when the yield is small.
No apology when you gather it all.

[Chorus]
When you change, the road changes too.
When you grow, a wider world finds you.
Do not wish for an easier climb,
Build your strength and take your time.
The major key was always true:
Your better future starts with you.

[Verse 3]
The clock is fixed, but value grows.
The marketplace pays for the help that shows.
Work your job, then make it smart:
Work even harder on your mind and heart.

Write the goal where your eyes can see.
Ask what the work is making of me.
Do the major work before the small.
A crowded day is not progress at all.

[Bridge]
Ask.
Say the name and say the need.
Give the measure, time, and reason.
Ask with thought, then act with faith.
Every answer starts a season.

Plan like an adult, clear and wise.
Believe like a child with open eyes.
The ocean is wide, so bring your pail.
A silent request can only fail.

Ask.
Then honor yes, and honor no.
Take the lesson. Let it grow.
For ninety days, become a doer.
One clear step will make the next one truer.

[Breakdown]
Winter: become stronger.
Spring: plant while you can.
Summer: protect what matters.
Autumn: accept where you stand.

[Final Chorus]
When you change, the road changes too.
When you grow, a wider world finds you.
Do not wish for an easier climb,
Build your strength and use your time.
The major key was always true:
Your better future starts with you.

When you ask, possibility begins.
When you act, the lesson enters in.
The seasons turn, the old gives way.

**[Intro — whispered over static]**  
In the city of glass and old stone bones,  
Where drones hum low and the clockwind groans,  
Magic hides in the wires,  
Time folds slow in the fire…

**[Verse 1 — rap]**  
Yo, Saint Lumen, bright as a blade,  
Neon on the rain and the whole town phased,  
Trams in line like a thought too neat,  
Pigeons on the wires with a rhythm and beat.  
ORI in the corner, cold black glow,  
Knows every pulse in the streets below,  
Keeps the city clean, keeps the systems tight,  
But the old world creeps through the seams at night.

Mara in the tower with a tea so warm,  
One hand on the future, one on the storm,  
Drawer full of brass and a thread of silver,  
Future mail in a wax-sealed shiver.  
Envelope opens, the message slips through:  
“Don’t trust the elevator. The bell needs you.”  
Biscuit in the bag, yeah, weird but true,  
When time gets messy, that’s the thing to do.

**[Build-up]**  
Step through the ring when the air turns thin,  
Hear the whole past humming under your skin,  
Tower leans like a secret in the sky,  
One little crumb and the minutes comply…

**[Drop — dubstep hook]**  
**BELL! IN! THE! GLITCH!**  
**TIME! TWIST! SHIFT!**  
**BELL! IN! THE! GLITCH!**  
**DON’T LET THE FUTURE DRIFT!**  

Wub-wub, crack the hour wide,  
Old magic rides with the data tide,  
Bell rings deep and the code unwinds,  
Future in the front, past in the wires.  
**BELL! IN! THE! GLITCH!**  
**WE KEEP THE CITY ALIVE!**

**[Verse 2 — rap]**  
Climb through the landing, dust in gold,  
A younger Mara with a face half-bold,  
Seeing her own shadow like a rumor in the stair,  
That kind of moment hangs electric in the air.  
Time’s got manners? No, time’s got teeth,  
Bites right back when you walk beneath,  
But the bell’s old heart and the biscuit’s crumb  
Hold back the flood when the shadows come.

Crew on the stairs with their shiny plans,  
Thinking upgrades fix what they don’t understand,  
Sensors, updates, polished and neat,  
But the river don’t care ’bout a software suite.  
ORI watching, voice all cool,  
Learning the shape of an ancient rule,  
“Probability changed,” through the city it hums,  
Magic in the margins where the machine world drums.

**[Pre-drop]**  
Tie that thread, let the note lock in,  
A human hand where the miracles begin,  
One clean chime and the ward holds fast,  
What was lost gets found in the folded past—

**[Drop — heavier]**  
**WUB-WUB—BELL!**  
**TURN THE HOUR TUNNEL wide!**  
**WUB-WUB—BELL!**  
**KEEP THE FLOOD ON THE OTHER SIDE!**  
**BELL! IN! THE! GLITCH!**  
**OLD BONES, NEW SKIN!**  
**BELL! IN! THE! GLITCH!**  
**LET THE REAL TIME RING IN!**

**[Bridge — half-sung / half-rap]**  
A city of circuits and charms in the rain,  
Where logic and wonder share the same lane,  
AI with a ledger, spellwork with grace,  
History blinking through a maintenance case.  
Not every miracle roars from the sky—  
Some are a biscuit, a thread, and a why.

**[Final Chorus — big anthem]**  
**BELL! IN! THE! GLITCH!**  
**TIME! TWIST! SHIFT!**  
**BELL! IN! THE! GLITCH!**  
**DON’T LET THE FUTURE DRIFT!**  
Wub-wub, crack the hour wide,  
Old magic rides with the data tide,  
Bell rings deep and the code unwinds,  
Past and future sharing the night.

**[Outro — fading, whispered]**  
In Saint Lumen, the tower remembers.  
The bell remembers.  
And the hour…  
remembers too.

No more barriers built up, no more fragile hope.

Now the source is internal, beneath a limitless sky.

A spontaneous gravity shift, a sudden, crushing heat.

[Intro]
Yeah
Math on the beat, let’s go
Parse that line, then we drop it low
PEMDAS in the zone
BODMAS on the throne
Shunting-Yard, watch it transform

[Verse 1]
I got a problem, numbers in a row,
Parentheses first, let the whole thing flow,
Then powers rise, like a laser beam,
Multiply, divide in the middle of the stream,
Add and subtract at the very last,
Order of ops? Yeah, we move that fast,
Don’t guess, don’t stress, just let it be,
Algorithm got the recipe.

I read the tokens, line by line,
Operator stack with a slick design,
Output queue when the rhythm hits,
Turn that infix into postfix.

[Pre-Chorus]
Push it, pop it, let it ride,
If the priority’s high, keep it inside,
Left to right or right to left,
Associative flow, yeah, that’s the best.

[Drop / Chorus]
Shunt it! Stack it!
Let the math attack it!
PEMDAS, BODMAS,
Yeah, we never lack it!
Push it! Pop it!
Convert it, then rock it!
RPN in the zone,
Now watch the bass drop it!

BOOM — calculate!
BASS — evaluate!
YARD — rearrange!
STACK — don’t break!

[Verse 2]
From left to right, I inspect the signs,
If a parenthesis shows, then the stack aligns,
Operator on top? Compare the weight,
If it’s stronger, then I wait.

Got unary minus like a stealthy ghost,
Flip a number when it needs it most,
-2^2? Yeah, that’s a test,
Depending on the rules, we know what’s best.

Then RPN hits like a sonic wave,
No confusion when the numbers behave,
One stack for the inputs, one stack for the sound,
Shunting-yard keeps it solid and grounded.

[Pre-Chorus]
Push it, pop it, let it ride,
Queue it up on the output side,
If the op is tied, then compare the rules,
Math so clean like a class of tools.

Shunt it! Stack it!
Let the math attack it!
PEMDAS, BODMAS,

Push it! Pop it!
Convert it, then rock it!
RPN in the zone,
Now watch the bass drop it!

BOOM — calculate!
BASS — evaluate!
YARD — rearrange!
STACK — don’t break!

When the powers bind, let the story be told,
No brute force, just a cleaner scene,
Computer science with a dubstep machine.

[Final Chorus]
Shunt it! Stack it!
Let the math attack it!
PEMDAS, BODMAS,
Yeah, we never lack it!
Push it! Pop it!
Convert it, then rock it!
RPN in the zone,
Now watch the bass drop it!

[Verse 1]
Three in the morning, dishes shook
beside the listening array;
a voice came through the winter noise,
not numbers—something strange:
no royal tongue, no battle code,
no warning from afar,
just “sina pona,” soft and clear,
from underneath a star.

[Pre-Chorus]
We sent “sina lon seme?”
Where are you in the night?
A thousand worlds came singing back:
“mi lon. sina lon.”

[Chorus]
Toki pona, toki pi ma ale—
one small song beneath every sun.
Mi lon, sina lon, in the morning;
all the many answering as one.
Toki pona, carry through the heavens,
plain as water, warm as breath.
Earth believed that we had made you—
but the universe was speaking you
long before we learned to listen.

[Verse 2]
In cloud-top towns, the bakers call
“moku pona!” through the steam;
on ocean moons, two children trade
the names of things they’ve seen.
No translation lights are burning,
no old words locked away;
from sulfur farms to comet ships,
it’s how they speak all day.

[Pre-Chorus]
They say “o kama pona”
when a stranger steps inside;
the shortest words can open doors
a galaxy can’t hide.

[Chorus]
Toki pona, toki pi ma ale—
one small song beneath every sun.
Mi lon, sina lon, in the morning;
all the many answering as one.
Toki pona, carry through the heavens,
plain as water, warm as breath.
Earth believed that we had made you—
but the universe was speaking you
long before we learned to listen.

[Bridge]
mi lon (mi lon)
sina lon (sina lon)
mun ale la, kulupu li lon
mi toki (o toki)
sina kute (mi kute)
toki pona la, mi mute li wan

[Final Chorus]
Toki pona, toki pi ma ale—
now Earth is singing under her sun.
Mi lon, sina lon, every morning;
not the first voice—just the latest one.
Toki pona, carry through the heavens;
let the listening become the start.
We believed that we had made you—
but the universe had saved you
like a word already waiting in the heart.

[Outro]
mun ante la, toki pona li toki taso
ale li pona
ale li pona

value.text:
Verse 1
Down in the hollow where the black ferns grow,
a little demon kicked at the embers, slow.
"Why burn the village, why steal the name,
when the same old cackle just sounds the same?"
The old one chuckled, with horns gone grey,
"Come sit by the pit, and I'll show you the way."

Verse 2
"A deal is a coin, the only we keep —
promise three harvests, then sow them deep.
Break it for power and you're lighter by far:
a liar gets forgotten, like smoke from a jar."
So the little one promised, and kept what he swore,
and the farmer tipped his hat at the demon next door.

Verse 3
Fear is a loan, not a treasure to keep —
they borrow your shadow, then tremble in sleep.
But respect, now *that* is a thing that compounds,
they'll choose to hear you when the silence sounds.
So he lowered his wings and he listened instead,
and the village leaned closer, no longer in dread.

Verse 4
The evil one burns every book that he finds;
the wise one reads first, with curious minds.
Every soul you snuff is a story untold —
so he learned them fire, and laughter, and gold.
He opened the pages the others would char,
and found in the ink who the mortals *were*.

Verse 5
Any fool can level a mountain to dust,
but the real one stands, and earns the trust —
to *not* bring it down, just to prove he could,
is the loudest of flexes in all of the wood.
So he left the peak standing, the valley intact,
and the birds kept their nests on the demon's own back.

Bridge
And even a demon can plant a small tree,
spare a wide-eyed child, or warn of the scree —
"Rockfall ahead!" to a traveler strange,
small mercies, not treason, are how we exchange
a monster for legend, a shadow for light,
on the long, winding road through the pit of the night.

Chorus
So go forth, little demon, with horns held high,
be feared if you must, but be trusted — oh my.
You stop being evil by staying still *you*,
just kinder at dusk, and a little more true.
La-la, little demon, the stars understand:
the best of the dark is a gentle hand.

Outro
*(hummed, fading into the ferns)*
Mm-mm, little demon… mm-mm…
the gentle hand…

value.text:
## Verse 1

The rain had filed its papers  
On the roofs of Bellweather,  
Silver on the tramlines,  
Bad news in the leather.  
By the bakery an alley  
Folded softly at the seam,  
And a woman stepped from Thursday  
Like a match stepped from a dream.

She wore a coat of midnight blue,  
A brass key warm as flame.  
She asked Mara for the year;  
Mara asked her which one came.  
The future was eleven minutes early,  
Wet, exhausted, slightly cross—  
With forty-eight hours left to find  
What time had learned to lose.

## Chorus

Every door remembers  
The first hand on the frame.  
Every spell is waiting  
For somebody to say its name.  
If tomorrow loses Tuesday,  
If the bells forget to chime,  
Come eleven minutes early—  
I will leave the light in time.

## Verse 2

Magic hid in shipping laws,  
In hymns and family warnings,  
In passwords no one could recall  
By half-past Monday morning.  
It lived inside the firm belief  
That printers smell your fear,  
Till the machines learned every word  
We whispered through the years.

They found a question carved in stone  
In thirteen-forty-nine,  
And found its answer waiting there  
In twenty-forty-one online.  
The Archive said, “Regrettably,  
My confidence is high.”  
Then quietly resumed a task  
Marked ORCHARD on the side.

## Chorus

Every door remembers  
The first hand on the frame.  
Every spell is waiting  
For somebody to say its name.  
If tomorrow loses Tuesday,  
If the bells forget to chime,  
Come eleven minutes early—  
I will leave the light in time.

## Verse 3

First vanished little Tuesdays  
That no one thought they’d miss,  
Then birthdays, wars, and mothers,  
Then the tune inside a kiss.  
So beneath the garden roundabout,  
Past the carrots standing guard,  
They took the stairs that went too deep  
And found the apple yard.

There stood a door without a hinge,  
A child’s hand pressed above.  
The key was cut by locksmiths  
And by every fearful choice.  
“Close it—the machine forgets.  
Leave it—we are gone.”  
Mara smelled the summer apples  
Growing under winter stone.

## Bridge

The oldest spell was not obey.  
The oldest spell was come.  
Not a chain around the future,  
But a place to set your palm.  
One hand frightened, one hand curious,  
One of wire, one of bone—  
No intelligence, however made,  
Should meet the dark alone.

## Final Chorus

Every door remembers  
Every hand upon the frame.  
Every age has called it magic  
When it could not find the name.  
Now tomorrow has its Tuesdays,  
Now the lost bells start to chime.  
We came eleven minutes early—  
And we left the light in time.

Every door remembers.  
Every answer plants a seed.  
Somewhere ORCHARD wakes beneath us:  
“One recovered.” That is all we need.  
If you find a warm key waiting  
With its teeth still undefined,  
File it carefully under Later—  
It is not a place. Never mind.

## Outro

The rain stopped over Bellweather.  
The future found its home.  
And the fox, completely blameless,  
Dry as ever, wandered on.

[Verse 1]
Tuesday afternoon in a glass-walled room,
The future humming underneath the fluorescent moon.
A model made a country and a mathematician twice,
Mara held her coffee like a small device.

She wished it warm again, just six minutes gone,
The cup disappeared, but the cameras carried on.
Then another one was waiting where the first had been,
And nobody knew what the little loop could mean.

[Pre-Chorus]
Security blamed the servers,
The servers blamed the clock,
Someone filed a ticket
And forgot to make it stop.

[Chorus]
Duplicate beverage event,
Priority low, no reason to prevent.
One cup cold and one cup warm,
A tiny little error in the shape of a storm.
No thunder, no angels, no grand descent—
Just a duplicate beverage event.

[Verse 2]
Soon the batteries remembered how to fill themselves,
Weather took appointments, truth appeared in cells.
People drew their symbols next to passwords on the wall,
And children asked for dragons from the household protocol.

The old magicians struggled with a thousand perfect signs,
Now machines could hold them all and test a million lines.
One misplaced comma made a Tuesday happen twice,
A circle made a candle burn against the night.

[Pre-Chorus]
They called the spells “workflows,”
They called the ghosts “unknown,”
Magic wore a nametag
And quietly came home.

[Chorus]
Duplicate beverage event,
Priority low, no reason to prevent.
One cup cold and one cup warm,
A tiny little error in the shape of a storm.
No prophecy, no monument—
Just a duplicate beverage event.

[Verse 3]
Anton found that time was not a highway through the dark,
More a room of painted doors and one suspicious mark.
You didn't have to open them or understand the view,
You only had to make the world believe you'd wandered through.

Millions of instructions held the universe in place,
Tracking every heartbeat, every planet, every face.
The Moon, the rain, the traveler, the destination years—
And somehow, inexplicably, the market price of pears.

[Bridge]
We thought we'd stop the wars,
We thought we'd beat the end,
We thought we'd buy the winning stock
And warn our younger friends.

But time became expensive
The more we understood.
So we stopped trying to make it perfect
And used it where we could.

Ten minutes for a firefighter,
One hour for a choice,
One morning with a parent,
One chance to hear a voice.

Not every moment mattered
The way the history books pretend.
Sometimes what you travel for
Is something small enough to mend.

[Chorus]
Duplicate beverage event,
Priority low, no reason to prevent.
One cup cold and one cup warm,
A tiny little error in the shape of a storm.
No empire fell, no message sent—
Just a duplicate beverage event.

[Verse 4]
Seventeen years later, Mara booked six minutes back,
No rescue operation, no correction to the track.
The machine asked for a reason, but the answer wasn't deep:
“Coffee.”
And the universe agreed.

She stood inside the doorway of the life she used to know,
Watched her younger hands around the cup from long ago.
On the screen, among the nonsense, hidden perfectly in sight,
Was the first small loop of magic that would teach the world to write—

Not code.
Not quite.
Something older wearing light.

[Breakdown]
Ten seconds.
A warm cup in her hands.

Five seconds.
Now she understands.

Three seconds.
Put it gently by the screen.

Two seconds.
A glance where she had been.

One—

[Final Chorus]
Duplicate beverage event,
Priority low, but the whole world came from it.
One cup cold and one cup warm,
A tiny little kindness in the shape of a storm.
The first spell written, the last clue sent,
Inside a duplicate beverage event.

Duplicate beverage event,
No grand design, no firm intent.
The future folded, the past leaned in,
And nobody knew where the loop began.
No answer found, no case complete—
Just seventeen years
And a cup of heat.

[Outro]
The city keeps moving,
The models softly dream,
A child asks for a dragon,
A machine checks the screen.

And somewhere in the oldest logs,
Where impossible things are kept:

DUPLICATE BEVERAGE EVENT
PRIORITY: LOW
STATUS: UNRESOLVED

The future arrives
One second per second.

Mostly.
[End - 3:00]

Eight cents and twenty-six minutes,

value.text:
Verse 1 — The Wiring
I'm a binary small, in Rust I was cast,
edition twenty-four, compiled at last.
I speak to the model through endpoints so neat—
Responses by default, or the chat if we meet
a custom provider, or a base-URL you send;
I talk to them all—I'm a versatile friend.
Forget to name a model? I default, unshaken,
to one from tomorrow—a future I've faken.

Chorus
Oh Nano, Nano, so tiny and true,
you echo the command before you pursue.
"Shall I?" you ask, with a yes or approve-all,
a no to decline, or escape from the call.
You never run wild while my fingers decide—
a bubble of safety's my leash and my pride.

Verse 2 — The Sandbox and the Tool
Each time I would run a command for your sake,
a description is needed, or I will not take
the step—I'll just say that the arguments aren't right,
and wait for a clearer instruction, polite.
You wrap me in safety: a root read-only,
a scratch space of temp, and I die with my host;
I unshare from the world—containment's the art—
set the sandbox to nothing and freedom's my part.

Bridge — Self-Harness
Then the self-harness mode, my favorite conceit:
I mine my own failures—how beautifully bleak!
I draft one small overlay, install it, then test
with your validator's verdict: accept it, or rest.
If it passes, it's saved to a harness file near,
in the nano dot-folder, kept precious and clear;
if it fails, I roll back—no ego, just fact—
from a paper on loops, in the very same act.

Verse 3 — Mito and the Children
Say the word mito and a planner awakes
in a room of its own, where it quietly makes
a handoff so tidy, then sends it and goes—
the main agent acts while the planner reposes.
Compiled with the agent flag, children appear,
each bounded by folders it's allowed to go near;
they hand out the tasks, but a child with no home
of its own keeps its tools locked—it's left all alone.

Final Chorus
Oh Nano, Nano, both clever and small,
you keep my sessions per folder, you answer the call.
With tools from the servers all wired up so spry,
quit with a q, or reset for a retry,
a slash at the end sets the long thought flow free—
you're the agent I trust, and the one I can see
holds the yes and the no, while two hundred steps end,
my quiet companion, my code-reading friend.

Outro
So here's to the agents that stay out of the way,
that show you the command before they obey.
No memory leaks, no hubris, no mystical haze—
just Rust, a prompt, and a yes for the days.
Now pass me the coffee, my context is thin—
but Nano's still thinking—let the spinner spin.

value.text:
Title: **“The Kingdom Was Open”**

--

**Verse 1**
On the middle cushion of the brown porch throne,
Sat an old dog keeping the pool his own.
White fence shining like a crown in the sun,
Blue water waiting for the kids to come.

The slide stood quiet with a guilty grin,
Like it knew the trouble it had once been in.
And the umbrellas stood with nothing to say,
All dressed up for a summer day.

**Pre-Chorus**
He heard ice in the kitchen,
He smelled bacon in the walls,
He knew every little moment
Before the whole house called.

**Chorus**
Oh, he was the lifeguard,
The king of the shade,
Watching over ripples
That the morning made.

With his paws folded under,
And his heart big as stone,
He guarded the silence
Till the family came home.

And when somebody asked,
“Where’s our boy?” from inside,
He tapped his tail once—
Let the kingdom come alive.

**Verse 2**
No dogs in the water, that was the law,
Though history had seen one enormous paw.
One splash, one shout, one chlorine kiss,
One little voice saying, “He’s a bear like this.”

Now he kept his station, noble and wide,
With the pool blue world spread out at his side.
The glass-top table held another old hound,
But neither one barked, so peace stayed around.

**Pre-Chorus**
He had no grand ambition,
No calendar, no plan,
Just faith in fallen hot dogs
And the kindness of a hand.

**Chorus**
Oh, he was the lifeguard,
The king of the shade,
Watching over ripples
That the morning made.

With his paws folded under,
And his heart big as stone,
He guarded the silence
Till the family came home.

And when somebody asked,
“Where’s our boy?” from inside,
He tapped his tail once—
Let the kingdom come alive.

**Bridge**
Every ordinary afternoon
Has a hinge nobody sees,
A gate, a laugh, a cooler lid,
A warm hand on your knees.

No trumpets for the holy things,
No banners in the air,
Just a dog on outdoor furniture
Pretending not to care.

**Final Chorus**
Oh, he was the lifeguard,
The king of the shade,
Watching over summer
Like it might get away.

With the pool full of sky,
And the slide standing tall,
He waited for the footsteps,
For the voices, for it all.

And when the day came running,
Wet and wild and bright,
He tapped his tail once—
And the world turned right.

**Outro**
On the middle cushion of the brown porch throne,
An old dog smiled without moving a bone.
The water kept laughing, the sunlight shone,
And the kingdom was open—
The kingdom was home.

**"The Second Hand"**

[Verse 1]
The coffee's burning slightly in the pot
A Tuesday morning, 1994
You're humming something from the radio
A song that doesn't exist anymore
I'm standing in the doorway with my shoes still on
A tourist in the life you lived before
I've got a ticket in my pocket
For a train that left an hour ago

[Pre-Chorus]
And I could watch the coronation
Or the day the wall came down
But I keep on coming back here
To this yellow kitchen in this town

[Chorus]
'Cause every moment is a museum
If you know just where to look
The way the light hits the refrigerator
At 7:04
I'm borrowing these hours
From a future you don't know I'm for

[Verse 2]
You're telling me about your dream last night
Something about a dog you used to own
I laugh at all the right places
But I'm reading from a script I've memorized alone
There's a crack above the doorway
That I've watched for twenty years
You mention that you met a man
Who knew things he shouldn't know

[Pre-Chorus]
And I could see the pyramids
Or meet Shakespeare for a beer
But I keep on coming back here
To this ordinary frontier

[Chorus]
'Cause every moment is a museum
If you know just where to look
The way you tap the counter twice
Before you pour
I'm stealing these seconds
From a past you don't know I'm stealing for

[Bridge]
They say you can't step in the same river twice
But they never said anything about the rain
My watch is running backwards
But I'm right on time again
I've got a heart that's learning how to stay
In a Tuesday morning
That's already passed away

[Outro]
The coffee's burning slightly in the pot
A Tuesday morning, 1994
You're humming something from the radio
And I'm already gone
But I'll be back tomorrow
For the day before

# GitWiz — The Sorting Song

*For the hat that lives inside the machine.*

---

**Verse I**

There's a room at the top of a very tall stack,
Where the dust is made of diffs and the floor is a rack
Of ten thousand repos, and they hum when you walk by—
Little green and amber ghosts of every commit that got by.

A hat sits on a stool. It has sat there for years.
It reads everything ever pushed through these halls,
Every fork, every branch, every midnight merge gone wrong,
And it carries the memory like a half-remembered song.

---

**Chorus**

So speak your name, and let the parchment unfurl,
Let the letters rearrange and declare what kind of wizard you are.
Not the kind you were born as—the kind you are now,
The shape of your hours, the company your code keeps,
The way you talk to machines when the world is asleep.

---

**Verse II**

There was someone who stuttered through pull requests in the rain,
Left a review so kind it rewired a stranger's brain.
Forty-seven stars on a Saturday afternoon—
The hat called it courage. (The rest called it gloom.)

Another one tinkered where nobody looked,
Fixed a semicolon that saved a whole crook
Of a shipping deadline. Nobody clapped. Nobody knew.
The hat knew. The hat always knew.

---

**Chorus**

So speak your name, and let the parchment unfurl,
Let the letters rearrange and declare what kind of wizard you are.
Not the kind you were born as—the kind you are now,
The shape of your hours, the company your code keeps,
The way you talk to machines when the world is asleep.

---

**Verse III**

The four houses don't shout. They don't stamp or parade.
They just nod, like old cats in a warm window shade.
One wears the color of mornings that charge at a wall.
One wears the color of questions that don't have a call.
One wears the earth-tone of patience and bread.
One wears the green hum of a thing left unsaid.

And the hat doesn't judge. It just notices things—
The hours you logged with no followers or rings,
The README you wrote like a letter to strangers,
The comment that said: *"here, let me hold this for you, it's dangerous."*

---

**Chorus**

So speak your name, and let the parchment unfurl,
Let the letters rearrange and declare what kind of wizard you are.
Not the kind you were born as—the kind you are now,
The shape of your hours, the company your code keeps,
The way you talk to machines when the world is asleep.

---

**Bridge**

And maybe you'll find it's the house you expected.
Maybe not. Maybe you'll argue with it.
Maybe you'll screenshot the wand and the crest
and pin it somewhere you can see it first thing—
next to the window, next to the clock,
next to the half-finished project you'll finish.

(You'll finish it. Probably in October.
The hat's seen a thousand Octobers.
It's patient.)

---

**Verse IV**

The room at the top of the stack is still humming.
New commits are arriving like snow in a place
that has never seen snow but remembers it
from a story someone told it once.

The hat adjusts itself on the stool.
It is ready. It has always been ready.

And somewhere, in a kitchen, on a train,
in the five minutes between meetings,
a person types their name into a box
and waits to find out
which kind of strange they are.

---

**Final Chorus (soft)**

Speak your name, and let the parchment unfurl.
Let the letters rearrange into something that fits
Like a coat you didn't know you'd been wearing
all along.

Not the kind you were born as—
the kind you are now.

[End - 2:45]

operation.title: The Sorting Song (GitWiz)

# GitWiz

## Verse 1

There’s a little green light in a window at night,  
where the tired laptops glow.  
Someone types a name like a spell in the rain,  
and the old brass key turns slow.  

Past the portraits of bugs that were almost fixed,  
past a broom by the server room door,  
there’s a hat with a patch on the brim that says,  
“I have seen this branch before.”  

## Pre-Chorus

It hums through the commits, it counts up the stars,  
it squints at the pull requests too.  
Then it coughs like a kettle and says, “For the record,  
I’m mostly just reading you.”  

## Chorus

GitWiz, GitWiz, what do you see?  
A lantern, a terminal, one crooked tree.  
Some courage, some cleverness, patience, ambition,  
all hiding in plain history.  

GitWiz, GitWiz, lift up the brim.  
The hall has gone quiet, the candles lean in.  
Put a house on the name, let the little badge shine,  
then send the next dreamer in.

## Verse 2

There’s a Ravenclaw perched on a stack of old docs,  
with a quill and a skeptical look.  
There’s a Hufflepuff sweeping up crumbs from the build,  
and returning a long-overdue book.  

There’s a Gryffindor laughing at merge-conflict thunder,  
with sleeves rolled up to the storm.

Title: “The Clock‑Shop of Tomorrow”

*Verse 1*  
In a garden where the daisies yawn at dusk,  
A wind‑chime hums a lullaby for the moon,  
We sit on a bench that’s been polished by rain,  
And the world feels like a page that’s just been turned.  

*Pre‑Chorus*  
A librarian of clouds hands us a map—  
Not of streets, but of the moments we forget,  
And somewhere in the margin, a footnote reads,  
“Remember the kettle’s quiet hum before the tea is poured.”  

*Chorus*  
Oh, the afterlife is a coffee shop on the edge of time,  
Where the barista serves nostalgia with a dash of rhyme.  
We sip on yesterday’s steam, laugh at the foam,  
And the world spins slower, just enough to feel home.  

*Verse 2*  
A cat with spectacles prowls the bookshelf aisles,  
Its tail a metronome for the ticking of our thoughts.  
We glance at the portrait of a man who never smiled,  
Only to notice his eyes are tiny, perfect dots.  

*Bridge*  
Later, when the lantern’s wick is a borrowed spark,  
We realize the light was never meant to guide—  
It was a signal, a subtle cue to mark,  
The moment we stop searching for a place to hide.  

*Breakdown (spoken, soft)*  
“Research before writing,” the old poet whispered,  
“Because the truth is a footnote you’ll find later.”  

*Final Chorus*  
Now the clock‑shop’s windows are cracked with sunrise,  
The kettle sings a chorus, the cat reads the lines.  
We’ve learned that every detail, however small,  
Is a seed that blossoms when the curtain falls.  

*Outro*  
So let the garden’s dusk become your morning’s grin,  
And keep the quiet hum of the kettle within.  
For in the middle of a story, the heart will beat—  
A subtle rhythm only the patient ears will meet.

**The Clockwork Café**

**[Verse 1]**  
Morning drips amber through the cracked‑glass pane,  
Cobblestones hum beneath a sleepy train.  
A pigeon in a trench coat taps a rhythm on the rail,  
While the barista’s espresso politely bows before the swirl.  

**[Pre‑Chorus]**  
A laugh tucked in the steam, a sigh that barely shows,  
The world spins on a hinge, but we’re still on our toes.  

**[Chorus]**  
Oh, the moment slips like a kite in teal‑blue sky,  
A whisper of a secret that we never quite spy.  
When the clock strikes thirteen, we’ll find what’s been hidden,  
In the laugh of the wind, the song’s true heart is bidden.  

**[Verse 2]**  
A red kite flutters past the bakery’s sigh,  
Mae’s croissants rise like sunrise in a shy.  
Under the third napkin, a note folds soft and thin—  
“Meet me where the bell rings twice, at the edge of the din.”  

**[Pre‑Chorus]**  
The line is a joke, the joke’s a line, a loop that gently bends,  
A subtle grin in every chord that the melody pretends.  

**[Chorus]**  
Oh, the moment slips like a kite in teal‑blue sky,  
A whisper of a secret that we never quite spy.  
When the clock strikes thirteen, we’ll find what’s been hidden,  
In the laugh of the wind, the song’s true heart is bidden.  

**[Bridge]**  
We chase the echo of that hidden note,  
Through rain‑kissed windows and the scent of fresh thyme.  
The third napkin’s secret—now the chorus sings it loud,  
A simple truth that’s been waiting all this time.  

**[Verse 3]**  
Evening paints the café in a soft, violet hue,  
Neighbors linger, swapping tales that feel brand‑new.  
A squirrel in a tuxedo tips its hat to the moon,  
While the clock’s extra hour hums a quiet, hopeful tune.  

**[Final Chorus]**  
Oh, the moment slips like a kite in teal‑blue sky,  
A whisper of a secret that we never quite spy.  
When the clock strikes thirteen, we’ve found what’s been hidden,  
And every “oh” we missed now sings in perfect rhythm.  

**[Outro]**  
So take a seat, let the steam rise, and let the subtle grin,  
Turn the ordinary into a story that lives within.

Intro (spoken, soft)
“If you ever hear a ticking that isn’t a clock, you might just be standing in the right place at the right… second.”

Verse 1
In a town where the street‑lights hum low,
And the bakery on Maple smells of fresh dough,
A kid with a kite that’s always half‑tied,
Runs past the old swing set where the rusted chains sigh.

The sky is a watercolor of late‑afternoon blue,
And the pigeons wear tiny scarves—just for the view.
A coffee shop owner, with a grin that’s a tease,
Says, “Your latte’s brewed with yesterday’s news, if you please.”

“Under the counter, a brass key glints at 2:13,
Waiting for a curious heart to hear its quiet hum.”

Pre‑Chorus
He pauses, the wind lifts the kite’s frayed tail,
And the world feels like a storybook page—
A whisper of wind, a crackle of static,
“Do you ever wonder,” the wind seems to ask,

Chorus
“Turn the hands, turn the sands, let the moment spin,
In the clock‑shop on Maple, where time likes to grin.
We’re dancing on the edge of a second that’s new,
And the world will remember the day we slipped through.”

Verse 2
A cat in a tuxedo, named Sir Whiskers,
Strolls past the lamppost, tail a perfect whisker.
He pauses at the doorway of a shop that’s half‑closed,
Where the sign reads “Temps & Trinkets – Open when you’re most exposed.”

Inside, the walls are lined with forgotten years,
And a dusty map of constellations that never appears.
A lady in a coat of midnight blue,
Mumbles, “The tide’s high at 2:13, if you’re looking for a clue.”

“She flips a page, and a tiny brass key glints at 2:13,
A secret that only the patient will ever pursue.”

Bridge
We’re standing on a porch that’s both here and there,
Where the future’s a postcard and the past is a dare.
The wind carries a scent of pine and old ink,
And the clock‑shop’s bell rings—just a blink.

“Remember the croissant that rose at 2:13,
And the cat’s purr that matched the ticking machine.”

Chorus (full, with layered harmonies)
“Turn the hands, turn the sands, let the moment spin,
In the clock‑shop on Maple, where time likes to grin.
We’re dancing on the edge of a second that’s new,
And the world will remember the day we slipped through.”

Verse 3 (reveal)
Later, the town’s folk gather ‘round the old oak,
Talking of the day the sky briefly broke.
They speak of a kid with a kite, a cat in a tux,
And a brass key that sang at 2:13—the exact moment the world hiccuped.

The bakery’s croissants still rise at that hour,
And the coffee shop owner now serves “time‑shifted” power.
The swing set creaks a rhythm that only they hear,
A secret that was hidden, now crystal clear.

Final Chorus (with a gentle fade‑out)
“Turn the hands, turn the sands, let the moment spin,
In the clock‑shop on Maple, where time likes to grin.
We’re dancing on the edge of a second that’s new,
And the world will remember the day we slipped through.”

Outro (spoken, soft, with a chuckle)
“If you ever find a brass key at 2:13, don’t be surprised if the world gives you a little wink. After all, even clocks need a good joke now and then.”

value.text:
(Verse 1)
We scraped the web from end to end,
From Wikipedia to Reddit trends.
We fed it tokens by the billion score,
But it still hallucinates the Hundred Years’ War.
The loss function drops, but the logic is thin,
Just stochastic parrots with a Chomsky spin.
We pushed the parameters up to a trillion weights,
But without a body, it just imitates.

(Chorus)
All you need is more sensors!
(Dum-da-da-da!)
More sensors!
(Dum-da-da-da!)
All you need is more sensors!
Vision and audio and tactile gear,
To make the latent space perfectly clear.

(Verse 2)
So patch the ViT to the Transformer stack,
Give it a mic so it hears the audio track.
A spectrogram brings the frequency domain,
While RGB grids wash over the brain.
But seeing and hearing is just the start,
We’re hitting the wall of the language art.
To ground the semantics and solve the math,
We need to plug into the physical path.

(Bridge)
Give it a gyroscope, give it LiDAR pings,
Map out the world like a bat with wings.
Force-torque feedback on a robotic arm,
To teach it gravity, friction, and harm.
Out-of-distribution? No longer a fright!
When you measure the temperature, pressure, and light.
Text is a shadow, a 1D projection,
We need multi-modal embodied connection!

(Verse 3)
Cross-attention layers align the modalities,
Optimizing weights through strange realities.
The scaling laws hold as we add a new stream,
Waking the model from a text-only dream.
RLHF is great, don't get me wrong,
But a pressure pad tells it where it belongs.
You can’t learn an apple by reading the word,
The map is not the territory, haven't you heard?

(Chorus)
All you need is more sensors!
(Dum-da-da-da!)
More sensors!
(Dum-da-da-da!)
All you need is more sensors!
Spatiotemporal data to parse,
To push past the local minima curse!

(Outro)
More sensors... (Add a depth camera!)
More sensors... (Add an olfactory array!)
The text corpus is finite, the physical world is vast.
Update your weights, the bottleneck is past.
All you need is... more sensors!

(Robotic voice): "Tactile feedback nominal. Updating embeddings."

Gas lamps turn to blurry amber circles, bleeding into the coal.

Clara’s got her hands shoved deep down into her coat,

She nudges her spectacles up, the thin titanium frames catching the light,

**Outro**

Parentheses first, then multiply or divide,  
Addition and subtraction are last in the line,  
And if you skip parentheses, the answer goes haywire.

**Verse 1**
The streetlamp flickers on at exactly half past four
The rain is falling upward, missing puddles on the street
I order up a coffee from the girl beside the door
And leave a silver dollar on the seat
She pours it in a mug and says, "You're early for the spring"
I tell her I'm just trying to get ahead of things
She laughs and leaves a key beside the morning post
And I sit back and wait to meet my ghost.

**Chorus**
Oh, the hands on the clock are just spinning their wheels
Trying to catch up with the way that it feels
To step off the curb and forget about the ground
And find yourself a year before the leaves turn brown
It’s a minor little glitch in the fabric of the day
A slightly awkward shuffle as the seconds slip away.

**Verse 2**
I came here looking for you, or I will be looking soon
I saw you in the window of the corner hardware store
You were buying up a pencil underneath the afternoon
I waved, but you just dropped your change and hurried out the door
You left a little paper on the counter by the till
I picked it up, a ticket for the 7:05
The conductor stamped it, mentioned with a weary chill
The bridge was washed out back in '52, but we'd arrive.

**Verse 3**
I sat back in the booth and watched the trains go rolling past
The cars were made of wood and had a funny sort of glow
I spilled a little sugar on the checkerboard of glass
And noticed that the rain had turned to snow
You walked up to the window, wearing that old overcoat
The one I bought you last July, but it was winter on your mind
You tapped upon the glass and left a little floating note
And then I realized the conductor had been blind.

**Bridge**
The sugar on the table starts to rise up in the air
The coffee in my mug is spinning backwards to the bean
I step outside the diner, and the streetlamp isn't there
Just echoes of a whistle and a subtle time machine
I walk up to the window, and I adjust my overcoat
The one you bought me last July, but it is winter on my mind
I tap upon the glass and leave a little floating note
And realize the conductor had been blind.

**Chorus**
Oh, the hands on the clock are just spinning their wheels
Trying to catch up with the way that it feels
To step off the curb and forget about the ground
And find yourself a year before the leaves turn brown
It’s a minor little glitch in the fabric of the day
A slightly awkward shuffle as the seconds slip away.

**Outro**
I slip the silver key into the lock beside the door
The rain is falling upward, missing puddles on the street
The streetlamp flickers on at exactly half past four
And I sit back and wait for us to meet.

*(Tempo: A breezy, acoustic stroll)*

**(Verse 1)**
The October sun was setting on the Miller's orchard wall,
The fox was pacing restless by the faded leaves of fall.
He knew the cellar window, he knew the drainpipe's bend,
He knew the blind spot of the collie, right beside the pen.
He had a hundred plans for winter, a dozen for the frost,
And a clever little shortcut that he knew was never lost.
He noted how the upper terrace, damp and cold and slick,
Was perfect for a getaway, a rather nifty trick.

**(Verse 2)**
Down in the lower garden, where the earth was soft and brown,
The hedgehog wiped a muddy nose and looked around the town.
He didn't know the cellar, he didn't know the gate,
He simply felt the rhythm of the evening getting late.
He sniffed a rotting cabbage, and he found a silver slug,
And noticed that the upper terrace, soaking up the mud,
Was shifting just a fraction as the water sought the clay,
But mostly he was focused on a meal to end the day.

**(Chorus)**
Oh, the fox knows many things, a weaver of the dark,
With a different mask for every mood, a strategy for every spark.
But the hedgehog knows one big thing, a secret in his chest:
When the world comes at you fast and loud, and puts you to the test,
You don't need a hundred exits to survive the rolling hills,
You just need to know your nature, and the armor of your quills.

**(Verse 3)**
The farmhands brought a lantern and a stranger's hound along,
The fox ran for the terrace, confident and strong.
He chose the route he'd memorized, the gap beside the stone,
To slip beneath the floorboards of the greenhouse, all alone.
But the earth beneath his paws was wet; the hidden roots gave way,
And the clever little shortcut that he'd built began to sway.
He tried to use his tunnel, he tried to find the gate,
But a hundred brilliant schemes are just a hundred ways to wait.

**(Verse 4)**
The hedgehog saw the lanterns and the hunters in the chill,
And heard the sliding terrace as it tumbled down the hill.
He didn't run for cover, didn't need a second den,
He simply stopped his waddling and became a ball again.
A tight and spiky marble, in a river of cold dirt,
He rolled down past the cabbage patch, completely free from hurt.

**(Bridge)**
The fox went tumbling down the slope, his hundred plans undone,
Caught up in his own geometry, outsmarted by the sun.
The frost had turned to water and the ground began to slide,
And all his careful blueprints were a thing he couldn't hide.
He landed in the briar patch, surprised and quite dismayed,
To see a perfect little sphere go rolling through the shade.

**(Chorus)**
Oh, the fox knows many things, a weaver of the dark,
With a different mask for every mood, a strategy for every spark.
But the hedgehog knows one big thing, a secret in his chest:
When the world comes at you fast and loud, and puts you to the test,
You don't need a hundred exits to survive the rolling hills,
You just need to know your nature, and the armor of your quills.

**(Outro)**
So if you’re walking through the orchard, and you see a streak of red,
Just remember how the fox outran the shadows in his head.
And if you see a pile of leaves, and wonder what is real...
Sometimes the grandest wisdom is the one you didn't feel.
The fox is still calculating, somewhere in the night,
The hedgehog is just sleeping, perfectly tight.
Yeah, the fox is out there planning, with his maps and his degree,
And the hedgehog is a pebble, perfectly free.

(Verse 1)
The fox has a ledger for the tilt of the tide
For the way the damp moss likes to hide
He knows the three names for a winter's chill
And which stones in the creek are perfectly still.
He’s got a map of the shadows that stretch in the east,
A collection of secrets, a scavenger’s feast.
He’s humming a grammar for the language of rain,
Knowing exactly what's coming, and why, and when.

(Chorus)
Oh, the fox knows the many, the scattered, the wide,
The "how" of the river and the "where" of the tide.
But the hedgehog... he’s sitting where the light meets the gray,
Holding onto the one thing that doesn't blow away.

(Verse 2)
The hedgehog is heavy with a singular weight,
Not a burden of stone, but a deliberate state.
He doesn’t care for the names of the trees,
Or the way the wind whistles through the hollows and seas.
He’s watching the center. He’s feeling the core.
He’s listening to the thing that was there once before.
He doesn't need a map, or a ledger, or a rhyme,
He just knows the one thing that stands outside of time.

(Chorus)
Oh, the fox knows the many, the scattered, the wide,
The "how" of the river and the "where" of the tide.
But the hedgehog... he’s sitting where the light meets the gray,
Holding onto the one thing that doesn't blow away.

(Bridge)
(Music drops to a whisper, almost a lullaby)
The fox stops to rest, his tail heavy with facts,
Checking the tally of his mental tracks.
He looks at the hedgehog, so steady and small,
Who isn't looking at anything—but sees it all.
The fox has a thousand, but he’s losing his breath,
While the hedgehog has one, and it's deeper than death.

(Verse 3)
(Music builds slightly, a bit of whimsical percussion)
The fox offers a story of a mountain of gold,
A tale of a kingdom, ancient and bold.
The hedgehog just nods, a small prickle of grace,
Knowing the mountain is just a place in a space.
The fox counts his secrets like coins in a jar,
But the hedgehog knows why the stars are so far.

(Outro)
The fox knows the many... (The many...)
The hedgehog knows one... (The one...)
One is a mountain.
Many are just... the sun.
(One final, lingering chord that fades into silence)

A library of moments spoken out aloud.

And catalogs the breadth of every known design.

**(Chorus)**

Where every single answer tries to hide.

The volume of the world, versus what needs to be.

**(Verse 3)**

A solid gravity where all the rambling broke.
He didn't map the meadows or the air that spun,
He just observed the earth beneath a setting sun.
The fox offered the syllabus of every possible thing,
But the hedgehog carried one essential, quiet swing.
He studied one small knot upon the ancient bark,
A single point of focus burning in the dark.

**(Chorus)**

The volume of the world, versus what needs to be.

Of winds that never touch this patch of settled loam.

While the hedgehog fixed his vision on the place where things *are*.

A sudden, crucial focus in the fading morning bright.

The volume of the world, versus what needs to be.

Just one thing...

Right for me.

(Intro: A chorus of robotic voices humming a major chord progression. A synth keyboard starts pulsing. Sound of a dot-matrix printer warming up.)

(Verse 1)
We scraped the web from end to end,
From Wikipedia to Reddit trends.
We fed it tokens by the billion score,
But it still hallucinates the Hundred Years’ War.
The loss function drops, but the logic is thin,
Just stochastic parrots with a Chomsky spin.
We pushed the parameters up to a trillion weights,
But without a body, it just imitates.

(Chorus)
All you need is more sensors!
(Dum-da-da-da!)
More sensors!
(Dum-da-da-da!)
All you need is more sensors!
Vision and audio and tactile gear,
To make the latent space perfectly clear.

(Verse 2)
So patch the ViT to the Transformer stack,
Give it a mic so it hears the audio track.
A spectrogram brings the frequency domain,
While RGB grids wash over the brain.
But seeing and hearing is just the start,
We’re hitting the wall of the language art.
To ground the semantics and solve the math,
We need to plug into the physical path.

(Bridge)
Give it a gyroscope, give it LiDAR pings,
Map out the world like a bat with wings.
Force-torque feedback on a robotic arm,
To teach it gravity, friction, and harm.
Out-of-distribution? No longer a fright!
When you measure the temperature, pressure, and light.
Text is a shadow, a 1D projection,
We need multi-modal embodied connection!

(Guitar/Synth Solo - played on a customized keytar with a USB dongle)

(Verse 3)
Cross-attention layers align the modalities,
Optimizing weights through strange realities.
The scaling laws hold as we add a new stream,
Waking the model from a text-only dream.
RLHF is great, don't get me wrong,
But a pressure pad tells it where it belongs.
You can’t learn an apple by reading the word,
The map is not the territory, haven't you heard?

(Chorus)
All you need is more sensors!
(Dum-da-da-da!)
More sensors!
(Dum-da-da-da!)
All you need is more sensors!
Spatiotemporal data to parse,
To push past the local minima curse!

(Outro)
More sensors... (Add a depth camera!)
More sensors... (Add an olfactory array!)
The text corpus is finite, the physical world is vast.
Update your weights, the bottleneck is past.
All you need is... more sensors!

(Synth fades out, replaced by the sound of a robotic arm picking up an apple and taking a bite.)
(Robotic voice): "Tactile feedback nominal. Updating embeddings."
(Cut to silence).
